livelox.heading: Put a training on Livelox
livelox.intro: Livelox shows the routes runners took, from their GPS watches or phones, on the map, so you can compare route choices after the training. Adding an event is free; you need a Livelox account.

download.title: Download the course data
download.body: Open the event, choose Print and then Download IOF XML under Course data. The file holds every course with its controls.

event.title: Create the event in Livelox
event.body: Log in at livelox.com and choose Manage › Event in the menu at the top, then Add an event. Fill in the name, the start time (the first start), the finish time (a little after the last runner is expected back) and the organising club, and save. Events in Eventor are created from Eventor instead.

map.title: Add the map
map.body: Under Maps, upload the club's map without the course on it: the OCAD file, or an image such as PNG. The map must be georeferenced; if it is not, Livelox lets you fit it onto a satellite image. Ask a club admin for the map file if you do not have it.

courses.title: Upload the courses
courses.body: Under Courses, choose Choose files to upload and pick the IOF XML file. Check the courses on the Preview tab. The file places the controls on the map but does not give their real-world coordinates yet, so if they are not in place, drag the control cloud onto the map as Livelox shows you. Save; Livelox offers to make a class for each course.

publish.title: Choose when the courses are shown
publish.body: The courses stay hidden until the event's start time. Under Access restrictions you can set a later publishing time, for instance after the last start, or limit the event to your club's members.

livelox.pdfNote: Do not upload the PDF from Print to Livelox as a course overlay: it has the map in it. Livelox draws the courses from the IOF XML file, without cut circles and lines, out-of-bounds markings or moved control numbers.
livelox.more: More in <docs>Livelox's own help on adding courses</docs>.

start.heading: Getting started
start.intro: Course setter is for setting orienteering courses on your club’s maps and printing them at the right scale. A club’s admins upload the maps once; members set courses in the browser and print them as PDFs.

club.title: Join or create your club
club.body: Someone in the club creates it under Your clubs and becomes its admin. Admins invite the others with a link from the club’s Members page (Create link); a link works for 14 days. A club can have several admins.

map.title: Upload the map (admins)
map.body: On Maps, upload the club’s OCAD file (OCAD 10, 11, 12 or 2018) or a PDF of the map. A PDF does not say its scale, so give the scale it is drawn at. Processing takes a minute or two. When the map is updated, upload the new file as a new version of the same map: events can then move to it with their controls kept in place.

event.title: Create an event
event.body: On Events, give the training a name and choose the map. An event is seen by the person who made it, the club’s admins and whoever they invite with Invite in the editor.

courses.title: Set the courses
courses.body: Choose New course, then Start, Control or Finish in the tool bar and click on the map. Controls are shared between courses: click a control that is already there to use it in this course too. Drag to move things; Ctrl+Z undoes. Fill in the control descriptions on the Descriptions tab, and add crossing points, marked routes and out-of-bounds areas from the tool bar. The print scale and the description size are chosen when printing. Everything is saved as you go.

print.title: Print
print.body: Choose Print. Drag the page over the map to choose what is printed, and the description sheet to a free spot; choose paper, orientation, scale and description size. Tick the courses to print, and All controls for whoever puts out the controls, then Make PDF. The PDF is ready to download in a few seconds to a minute.

start.printTip: Print the PDF at actual size (100 %). “Fit to page” or “shrink to fit” in the print dialog makes the map smaller, and then the scale is wrong.

livelox.title: Show the routes in Livelox
livelox.body: Download the course data as IOF XML from the print view and upload it to Livelox. See <livelox>how to put a training on Livelox</livelox>.

start.account: You can download what is stored about you, or delete your account, on Your account in the menu under your picture.
